messages:
andrea: Heads up — multiple GPU nodes in ap-southeast hitting intermittent DNS lookup failures since 02:00 UTC. Pods get `getaddrinfo: Name or service not known` when contacting model-registry.internal. Not all nodes; seems correlated with heavy outbound egress from batch jobs.

pat: saw that too. Telemetry shows spikes in NAT port reuse for that AZ. Conntrack table filling then ephemeral ports being reused, causing dns UDP replies to be mis-delivered? :thinking_face: 

maria: what's failing exactly — glibc getaddrinfo or systemd-resolved? can you paste `/etc/resolv.conf` from one affected node?

andrea: from affected node:
```
nameserver 169.254.20.10 # node-local-dns
search svc.cluster.local cluster.local
options ndots:5 timeout:2
```
But `ss -u -a` shows many sockets in TIME_WAIT to 53

leo: dig from node intermittently times out:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> model-registry.internal
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;model-registry.internal. IN A
;; Query time: 2000 msec
;; SERVER: 169.254.20.10#53(169.254.20.10)
;; WHEN: Thu Mar 4 02:04:12 UTC 2026
;; MSG SIZE  rcvd: 54
```
sometimes succeeds with 1ms.

pat: we're using iptables NAT from the egress LB that rewrites source ports. If the LB reuses source ports aggressively, it can collide with DNS UDP responses when conntrack is near cap.

maria: Can we check conntrack metrics? `conntrack -S` and kube-proxy conntrack-udp-timeout? Also check kubelet `--resolv-conf` flag — maybe it's pointing at stub listener which is overloaded.

andrea: conntrack entries hitting ~60k on some nodes, threshold is 65k. Also saw systemd-resolved CPU spikes. On-call suggests increasing conntrack max and reducing conntrack UDP timeout as short-term.

sre-oncall: @pat @andrea let's try workaround: 1) patch DaemonSet to set node-local-dns upstream to cluster-dns pod IPs 2) bump net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max to 200k 3) enable `dnsPolicy: Default` for hot batch pods to bypass node-local DNS and use host resolv for a minute — apply carefully.

leo: can we also reduce DNS UDP frag by enabling EDNS0? maybe not quick. Quick fix: roll egress LB config to preserve source port (if supported) or add per-node SNAT pool to avoid reuse.

pat: i can roll a conntrack bump now. maria can you push a node-local-dns image with aggressive cache TTL=1s? that should reduce outbound queries.

maria: pushed image tag `node-local-dns:fix-20260304-v2` to canary nodes in ap-southeast2. Monitoring logs.

andrea: after conntrack increase and canary node-local-dns, errors dropped to near-zero on canary nodes. Still seeing failures on older nodes; going to cordon/drain and rotate.

sre-oncall: plan: 1) roll conntrack sysctl cluster-wide 2) drain + update node-local-dns on remaining nodes 3) follow up with egress LB config review and tracelogging. If anyone has objections, shout now. Target complete in 2 hours.

pat: :thumbsup: I'll open an incident runbook and add postmortem checklist (check NAT port allocation, kube-proxy conntrack params, systemd-resolved upgrade).

devops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-3421 - DNS: intermittent UDP resolution failures — assigned to eng-infra. Runbook linked.

andrea: thanks all, will post updates. next: add longer-term fix: node-local-dns sticky connections or tcp fallback for critical services + metrics to alert when query latency > 500ms.
